region: Lima, Arequipa and the Colca Canyon, Lake Titicaca, Cusco, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu
title: Peru — Down the Colca, Across Titicaca, Up to Machu Picchu
subtitle: A staged climb from the Pacific coast to a condor canyon, a lake homestay and the Inca valleys, timed for the end of the rains
summary: Fifteen days from Lima to Arequipa, the Colca Canyon, Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu by flight, bus, boat and rail, ordered so sleeping altitude rises before the trip peaks. Planned for early March, when the Inca Trail reopens but the Andean rains and strike risk still shape every day.
introduction: Fly to Lima for ceviche and sea air, then climb in stages: Arequipa at 2,335 m, the Colca Canyon where Andean condors rise past the rim at dawn, and a two-day walk to an oasis on the canyon floor. A daytime bus crosses the 4,500 m altiplano to Puno, and from there a boat reaches a family homestay on Amantaní in Lake Titicaca. Only then does the route reach Cusco, the terraces and salt pans of the Sacred Valley, and the train down to Machu Picchu. Everything is public transport, rail and short hired-driver days, with spare days for rain and strikes.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is a low-altitude desert trip with a rented vehicle and tents. This is the opposite: a high-altitude, public-transport journey through terraced valleys, a deep canyon and a lake at 3,800 m, where acclimatisation, rain and road blockades matter more than navigation and fuel.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: The standard Peru package flies in to Cusco and goes straight to Machu Picchu at altitude in a coach group. This plan starts low, walks into the Colca Canyon, sleeps with a family on Titicaca, and treats Machu Picchu as the end of the climb rather than the first stop.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination in the portfolio combines a canyon descent, an Aymara-Quechua island homestay and the Inca capital in one staged altitude route. Compared with Chile's Atacama (D20), which is a self-drive high desert, this route is cultural and valley-based rather than desert-based.

duration.note: Day 1 outbound and day 15 return; long-haul flights Paris-Lima and back, with domestic flights Lima-Arequipa and Cusco-Lima.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: The classic Inca Trail network is closed every February and reopens on 1 March, the rains are easing (but not over), and the dates fall before Semana Santa (22-28 March 2027, Easter Sunday 28 March) when Peruvian domestic travel peaks. February is the wettest month in the southern Andes.

februarySuitability.summary: Peak rainy season in Cusco and Puno, with the highest landslide, train and road-closure risk, Carnival (about 6-10 February) and the Puno Candelaria festivities, and the Inca Trail network closed for the whole month. Machu Picchu itself stays open.

marchSuitability.summary: Rains are easing but still frequent; the Inca Trail network reopens on 1 March (2026 pattern, 2027 not yet confirmed). The ENFEN outlook points to below-normal rain in the south-eastern sierra and Titicaca basin in summer 2027, but forecasts are uncertain. Early to mid March avoids Easter crowds.

climate.regionNote: Approximate climate normals combined for Arequipa, Chivay, Puno and Cusco; Lima is hotter and Colca/Puno colder. Planning ranges from general climate knowledge, not from a fetched dataset. Lima in March is warm and humid (about 26-29 °C).

february.rainfall: Heavy in Cusco and Puno (about 140-150 mm and 18+ rain days in February), light in Arequipa; coast is dry
february.humidity: High in Cusco and Machu Picchu; dry on the coast and Arequipa
february.notes: Frequent afternoon storms, mist at Machu Picchu, high landslide risk; February is the Inca Trail closure month (S09).

march.rainfall: Still wet in Cusco and Puno (about 100-120 mm), easing late in the month; light in Arequipa
march.humidity: High in cloud-forest areas around Machu Picchu
march.notes: Morning clear spells are common; the ENFEN outlook for summer 2027 points to deficits in the south-east sierra (S12).

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Passes near 4,500-4,900 m can see sleet or snow; rock- and mudslides can close Salkantay and Santa Maria-Santa Teresa routes to Machu Picchu in the rainy season (S04). The Sangalle trail can be slippery after rain.
climate.seaConditions: Pacific off Lima is cool and often hazy; strong El Niño conditions are forecast for the north and central coast (S12). Not part of the main activities.
climate.airQuality: Good in the highlands; Arequipa and Cusco have traffic and dust but no major seasonal haze. Ubinas volcano near Arequipa has emitted gas and ash (S04).
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Condors are seen at Cruz del Cóndor year-round, with morning thermals best in drier months; rains can reduce visibility. Highland birds and flowers are at their greenest.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Semana Santa and Easter
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: 22-28 March 2027 (Easter Sunday 28 March; Holy Thursday and Good Friday 25-26 March are national holidays)
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Avoided by the recommended window; return flight and Cusco hotels would book out later in the month.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Carnival and Virgen de la Candelaria in Puno
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: Carnival about 6-10 February 2027; Candelaria festival early February
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: February only: crowded Puno and Cusco, water-throwing games, higher prices.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Inti Raymi and high season
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Not relevant to the window; Machu Picchu uses a higher 5,600 daily cap in high season (S10).

climate.ramadan2027: Not relevant: Peru is overwhelmingly Christian and Ramadan does not affect services.
climate.tourismDemand: Low-to-shoulder season in February and March; Machu Picchu and trains are easier to book than in June to August, but Inca Trail permits for March are still the first to sell out because trekkers displaced from February rebook.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: February and early March are usually among the cheaper months for Europe-Lima fares; fares rise from late March (Easter) and into June-August.

geography.summary: The Pacific desert coast, the volcanic Arequipa basin, the 4,000 m altiplano with Lake Titicaca, the Colca Canyon, the Urubamba valley and cloud-forest edges at Machu Picchu.
geography.distinctive: The Colca Canyon plunges more than 3,000 m below the surrounding volcanic peaks, and Lake Titicaca lies at about 3,812 m, one of the highest navigable lakes in the world. The route steps through five distinct altitude bands in 15 days.

landscapes.name: Colca Canyon
landscapes.description: A deep river canyon with Inca and pre-Inca terraces, the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint and a green oasis on the floor.

landscapes.name: Lake Titicaca and its islands
landscapes.description: A high-altitude lake with the Uros reed islands and the farming islands of Amantaní and Taquile.

landscapes.name: Arequipa volcanic basin
landscapes.description: A white-stone city surrounded by the Misti, Chachani and Pichu Pichu volcanoes.

landscapes.name: Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu
landscapes.description: Terraced Urubamba valley with Moray, Maras and Ollantaytambo leading down to cloud forest at Machu Picchu.

culture.summary: Inca and pre-Inca sites, Quechua and Aymara communities, colonial convents and one of the world's most varied cuisines, from Lima ceviche to Arequipa picanterías.

culturalHighlights.name: Machu Picchu
culturalHighlights.description: The ridge-top Inca complex entered with a timed circuit ticket; the group visits with a licensed guide and a second option day.

culturalHighlights.name: Santa Catalina Monastery, Arequipa
culturalHighlights.description: A walled colonial convent of narrow blue and orange streets built in sillar stone.

culturalHighlights.name: Amantaní homestay
culturalHighlights.description: A night with a farming family on a car-free island, organised through the island's committee system; meals are part of the stay.

culturalHighlights.name: Taquile textile tradition
culturalHighlights.description: Island weaving and knitting listed by UNESCO; visited through the community-run system.

culturalHighlights.name: Moray and Maras, Sacred Valley
culturalHighlights.description: Circular terraces and working salt pans maintained by local families.

culturalHighlights.name: Lima's markets and cevicherías
culturalHighlights.description: Surquillo market, nikkei and Andean restaurants.

adventureHighlights.name: Colca Canyon descent to Sangalle
adventureHighlights.description: About 1,000 m down to an oasis and three hours back up, with a local guide; the track is slippery after rain and not suitable if the river is high.

adventureHighlights.name: Over the 4,900 m pass to Chivay and Puno
adventureHighlights.description: Two long daytime bus rides over high passes; altitude sickness is a real risk and the order of the route is designed around it.

adventureHighlights.name: Machu Picchu circuits and Huayna Picchu
adventureHighlights.description: Timed tickets; Huayna Picchu and Machu Picchu Mountain are stair-heavy and have caused fatalities (S05).

adventureHighlights.name: Optional Lares or Salkantay trek instead of the rail day
adventureHighlights.description: A 3-4 day trek over passes near 4,400-4,630 m; rainy-season landslide risk on Salkantay and the Santa Maria route (S04). Not in the base plan.

signatureExperiences.title: Condors and the Colca Canyon to the Sangalle oasis
signatureExperiences.description: Be at Cruz del Cóndor at first light for the condors, then walk down about 1,000 m to an oasis and sleep in the canyon.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Few trips combine condor watching and a canyon-floor night; the climb out gives a physical day without technical skill.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Base two nights in Chivay, take the early bus to Cruz del Cóndor, walk with a local guide and mule for bags. Book bungalow beds in advance.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Colca ticket, guide share, bungalow and local buses; estimate

signatureExperiences.title: Homestay on Lake Titicaca (Uros, Amantaní, Taquile)
signatureExperiences.description: A boat day to the Uros reed islands, a night with a family on Amantaní, and Taquile's weaving on the way back.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: An island homestay at 3,800 m run by committees, with a long evening of cooking and conversation rather than a coach stop.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book through a locally owned operator or the community boat system in Puno; ask what share goes to the host family; bring warm layers and cash.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Two-day package including homestay meals; estimate

signatureExperiences.title: Moray, Maras and Ollantaytambo by hired driver
signatureExperiences.description: One day in the Sacred Valley covering the circular terraces, the salt pans and an inhabited Inca town.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: These are working agricultural landscapes rather than monuments, and the day ends in a living Inca street grid.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Hire a van and driver for the day from Cusco, finish at Ollantaytambo and sleep there for the morning train.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Hired van share, tickets and lunch; estimate

signatureExperiences.title: Machu Picchu by train with a spare day
signatureExperiences.description: A timed circuit ticket with a guide, followed by a flexible day for a second visit or the cloud-forest waterfall walk.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Reaching the citadel after weeks of altitude and village stays, with a spare day built in for the rainy-season weather.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Buy tickets on tuboleto.cultura.pe as soon as the dates are fixed, book train seats on a changeable fare, and ask the guide for a circuit that matches the weather.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Train, ticket, shuttle bus and guide share, excluding hotel; estimate

travelStyle.summary: Buses, trains, boats and short hired-driver days, with two guided walking days. Self-drive is not planned.

transport.summary: Domestic flights Lima-Arequipa and Cusco-Lima, intercity buses (Arequipa-Chivay, Chivay-Puno, Puno-Cusco), boats on Titicaca, PeruRail or Inca Rail to Machu Picchu, and a hired van for the Sacred Valley.

modes.description: LATAM, Sky Airline and JetSMART serve Lima-Arequipa and Lima-Cusco; fares and schedules not verified.

modes.mode: Intercity buses and tourist day buses
modes.description: Daytime buses only on mountain roads; night buses are avoided because bus crashes and holdups are reported (S04). Companies such as Cruz del Sur serve Arequipa, Puno and Cusco.
PeruRail and Inca Rail run from Ollantaytambo and from the Cusco area; protests and landslides occasionally suspend the line (S04, S16).
Community and operator boats from Puno to the islands.

transport.carRental: Not used. Rental is possible in Lima, Arequipa and Cusco, but driving standards are poor, mountain roads are slow, rainy-season landslides and protest blockades make delays likely, and an international driving permit is advised (S04).

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-drive is possible but not recommended: poor driving standards, high-altitude mountain roads, landslides in the rainy season and blockades that cannot be crossed (S04).
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Peru accepts foreign licences for tourists; an international driving permit is commonly advised; confirm for the licence's issuing country.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four travellers hold car licences. Sharing driving would be allowed with an additional-driver rental contract, but this trip does not need it.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No one rides a motorcycle or scooter without the legally required licence. Legal alternatives: buses, hired drivers, taxis, tuk-tuk-style mototaxis as passengers, walking.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Use buses, rail, boats and hired drivers; keep a hired van to a single Sacred Valley day.

accommodation.summary: Mid-range hotels and guesthouses in cities, a family homestay on Amantaní and basic bungalows at the Sangalle oasis.

camping.summary: One night in bungalows or tent pitches at the Sangalle oasis; the rest is in hotels and a homestay. Camping gear is not required and not budgeted.

physicalDifficulty.label: demanding
physicalDifficulty.summary: Altitude is the main load: nights at 3,400-3,800 m, a pass near 4,900 m and a 1,000 m descent and climb at Colca. No technical skills needed, but altitude sickness, rain and long bus days make it demanding.

itinerary.summary: Lima for food, Arequipa and the Colca Canyon for acclimatisation and condors, Puno and Lake Titicaca for a homestay, then Cusco, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu, with two flexible days for rain and strikes.

days.title: Fly to the Pacific coast
activities: Land in Lima in the afternoon, official taxi to Miraflores
days.travelTime: ≈ 12-14 h direct; 16-20 h with one stop
days.culturalHighlight: Lima's food culture from the first evening
days.geographicalHighlight: Dry coastal desert on a cold Humboldt-current sea
days.practical: Flights are not verified; airport taxi via official desk or app only (S04).

days.title: Markets and the food day
activities: Optional Pachacamac or catacombs by day
days.practical: Avoid the historic centre after dark (French yellow zone); keep phones out on the street (S01, S04).

days.title: Up to 2,335 m
days.culturalHighlight: Santa Catalina convent in sillar stone
days.practical: First night above 2,000 m; no alcohol, drink water, slow pace.

days.title: Over the 4,900 m pass to the Colca valley
activities: Morning bus to Chivay with a photo stop at the pass
Check in, walk the market and terraces
Evening hot springs at La Calera
days.accommodation: Hotel or family hostel in Chivay
days.geographicalHighlight: Altiplano, volcanic skyline, pass near 4,900 m
days.practical: The pass is the highest point of the trip; sleep at 3,650 m. Bring warm layers and stay hydrated (S06).

days.title: Condors, then into the canyon
activities: Be at Cruz del Cóndor before 08:00
Descend about 1,000 m to the oasis
Swim and sleep in a bungalow or tent
days.transport: Early bus, then walking with a guide
days.travelTime: ≈ 1 h by road, 3-4 h walking down
days.accommodation: Basic bungalows or tent pitches at the oasis
days.geographicalHighlight: Colca Canyon, one of the deepest in the Americas
days.practical: Trek only in dry spells; river crossings and trail erosion are rainy-season hazards. Local guide advised (S04, S18).

days.title: Climb out and hot springs
activities: Climb about three hours to Cabanaconde
Hot springs if not done on day 4
days.practical: Mules can carry bags or a tired walker; leave a spare day buffer in the plan if the canyon track is wet.

days.title: Over the altiplano to Lake Titicaca
days.transport: Tourist bus or public bus via Juliaca
days.geographicalHighlight: Plateau at about 4,500 m, then Titicaca
days.practical: Travel by day only; protests and road blockades have repeatedly cut the Puno roads (S04, S19).

days.title: Reed islands and a homestay
days.practical: Bring cash and small gifts such as school supplies; no heating, nights are cold (S05).

days.title: Taquile and the day bus to the Inca capital
activities: Boat to Taquile and a short walk
Late-afternoon bus to Cusco (arrive after dark)
days.practical: Long day; a tourist bus with stops is safer than a night bus. Alternative: fly Juliaca-Cusco if weather or blockades close the road (S04).

days.title: Inca capital, slow day at 3,400 m
activities: Sacsayhuamán on foot or by taxi
days.practical: Free day to absorb the day-9 journey and altitude; swap with day 11 if the Sacred Valley is closed by rain or a strike.

days.title: Moray, Maras and a living Inca town
activities: Continue to Ollantaytambo and climb the fortress
days.practical: Landslides can close side roads in the rainy season; confirm the day before (S02, S08).

days.title: Train to Machu Picchu
activities: Shuttle bus up to Machu Picchu
Timed entry on circuit 2 with a guide
days.transport: PeruRail or Inca Rail, shuttle bus
days.practical: Rainy season: mist, mud, closed trails and possible train interruptions; check tuboleto.cultura.pe well ahead (S10, S16).

days.title: Spare day on the mountain, then rail back
activities: Second ticket for another circuit or the Mandor waterfall walk
Afternoon train to Cusco area, transfer to Cusco
days.culturalHighlight: Machu Picchu second visit or cloud-forest walk
days.practical: Flexible: this day absorbs cloud, landslide or train disruption on day 12; book rail changeable fares.

days.title: Fly out via Lima
days.travelTime: ≈ 1 h 30 min flight; ≥ 6 h buffer before the international departure
days.practical: Cusco flights are fog- and weather-sensitive; take the first morning flight and keep a long buffer.

days.title: Back in France
activities: Arrive in Paris in the morning
days.practical: Many Lima-Paris flights leave late evening and land the next morning, so day 15 is mostly the flight; confirm the schedule when booking.

stops.name: Jorge Chávez International Airport, Lima (LIM)
stops.description: Arrival and departure airport; Callao district around the terminal is a French yellow vigilance zone, so official or app taxis only.
activities: Taxi from the official desks or a ride-hailing app
Eat airside before the evening flight home
stops.transport: Official airport taxis; Metropolitano bus not recommended with luggage on arrival

stops.name: Lima - Miraflores, Barranco and Surquillo
stops.description: The food day: markets, cevicherías, anticuchos, Peruvian-Japanese (nikkei) and Andean cooking, on cliffs above the Pacific.
activities: Surquillo market breakfast and ceviche lunch
Barranco and the Miraflores clifftop path
Optional Pachacamac or historic centre by day, not after dark
stops.culturalImportance: Viceregal and republican Lima, plus pre-Inca sites such as Pachacamac
stops.geography: Dry coastal desert, 28-30 °C in March, humid
stops.accommodation: Mid-range hotel in Miraflores or Barranco

stops.name: Arequipa
stops.description: The white volcanic-stone city at 2,335 m under the Misti volcano; first night of the staged climb.
activities: Picantería lunch of rocoto relleno and adobo
stops.culturalImportance: Colonial city and convent in sillar stone, UNESCO historic centre
stops.geography: Semi-arid valley under Misti, Chachani and Pichu Pichu volcanoes
stops.accommodation: Guesthouse or hotel near the Plaza de Armas

stops.name: Chivay
stops.description: Market town of the Colca valley at about 3,650 m; base for hot springs and the climb to the Colca rim.
activities: Sleep two nights here around the canyon walk
stops.culturalImportance: Collagua and Cabana farming communities with ancestral terraces
stops.geography: High valley, terraced fields, alpaca pastures
stops.transport: Bus from Arequipa (about 3 h 30, via a pass near 4,900 m)

stops.name: Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint (Colca Canyon)
stops.description: Cliff viewpoint where Andean condors rise on morning thermals; coordinates approximate the Colca Canyon, not the exact viewpoint.
stops.culturalImportance: Condors are sacred to Andean peoples
stops.transport: Early bus or taxi from Chivay (about 1 h)

stops.name: Cabanaconde and the Sangalle oasis trek
stops.description: Village on the south rim and the path into the canyon: about 1,000 m down to an oasis with bungalows and a tent area, and about three hours back up.
stops.culturalImportance: Village life on the canyon rim
stops.geography: River oasis at the canyon bottom, palms, mountain streams
stops.transport: On foot with a local guide; mules for bags
stops.accommodation: Basic bungalows or tent pitches at the oasis

stops.name: Puno
stops.description: Lake city at about 3,820 m, the departure point for Titicaca; the lowest-risk way to arrive is by a daytime bus from Chivay.
activities: Evening walk along the lakefront with the group
Check the next day's boat and weather
stops.culturalImportance: Gateway to Aymara and Quechua island communities
stops.geography: Altiplano on the shore of Lake Titicaca

stops.name: Uros floating reed islands
stops.description: Communities living on rebuilt totora-reed islands near Puno, visited by boat.
activities: Ask for a community-run visit and buy crafts directly
stops.culturalImportance: Uros reed-island way of life; visit only with community guides
stops.geography: Reed beds in a high-altitude lake
stops.transport: Boat from the Puno harbour (about 30 min)

stops.name: Amantaní island
stops.description: Farming island with homestays organised by village committees; evening meals and a sunset hill walk.
activities: Homestay dinner with the host family
Sunset climb to the summit shrines
stops.culturalImportance: Quechua farming community with a rotating homestay system
stops.geography: Terraced hills on an island at about 3,800 m
stops.costNote: Included in the Titicaca package line

stops.name: Taquile island
stops.description: Island known for the knitting of its men and communal weaving, listed by UNESCO as intangible heritage.
stops.geography: Island with stone terraces and lake views
stops.transport: Boat from Amantaní (about 1 h), then Puno (about 2 h)

stops.name: Cusco
stops.description: Former Inca capital at about 3,400 m: stone-walled streets, markets and the Plaza de Armas; used as the base for the Sacred Valley and the return flight.
stops.culturalImportance: Inca capital with colonial cathedrals built on Inca foundations
stops.transport: Day bus from Puno; train from Aguas Calientes (to Poroy or Ollantaytambo); flight to Lima
stops.accommodation: Hotel in San Blas or the centre

stops.name: Moray terraces
stops.description: Circular Inca terraces on the Maras plateau, thought to have been an agricultural experiment.
activities: Combine with the salt pans on the same day
stops.transport: Hired van from Cusco or Chinchero

stops.name: Maras salt pans (Salineras)
stops.description: Thousands of small terraced evaporation pools fed by a salt spring and worked by local families.
activities: Buy salt directly from the cooperative
stops.culturalImportance: Working salt pans managed by local families
stops.geography: Mountain slope above the Urubamba valley

stops.name: Ollantaytambo
stops.description: Living Inca town with a fortress and terraces; the rail station for Machu Picchu.
stops.culturalImportance: Inca town plan with continuous habitation
stops.geography: Narrow side valley at about 2,790 m
stops.transport: Hired van; PeruRail or Inca Rail

stops.name: Aguas Calientes (Machu Picchu Pueblo)
stops.description: Town below Machu Picchu reached only by rail or on foot; sleep here to enter the citadel the next morning if the afternoon entry is full.
activities: Check the ticket time and weather
Mandor gardens and waterfall walk on the spare day
stops.culturalImportance: Gateway town to the Inca citadel

stops.name: Machu Picchu
stops.description: The Inca citadel on its ridge above the Urubamba, entered with a timed ticket for one of three circuits.
activities: Optional second ticket for a different circuit on day 13
stops.transport: Shuttle bus up from Aguas Calientes (about 25 min) or walk
stops.costNote: Entry ticket at agency-guide figure of about S/152 for a foreign adult; official site must be checked

budget.materialUncertaintyNote: Flight fares from aggregator snippets span roughly 730-1,240 EUR, so the realistic total could cross the 2,500 EUR line. A live fare quote for the exact dates is needed to resolve this.
budget.exceptionalJustification: The total sits in the exceptional band mainly because of the Paris-Lima long-haul fare (about 1,050 EUR of the headline) rather than local costs, which are about 1,360 EUR for 15 days including contingency. The trip adds Machu Picchu, the Colca Canyon and a Titicaca homestay, which have no cheaper equivalent elsewhere in the portfolio.

scenarioNotes.economical: Public buses, hostel rooms, cheap fares and fewer paid activities; assumes a cheaper flight and early booking.
scenarioNotes.realistic: Tourist day buses, mid-range hotels, Expedition-class train, one hired-driver day and a guided canyon walk and Machu Picchu visit.
scenarioNotes.comfortable: Vistadome rail, better hotels, private guides and a higher fare.

security.summary: The route avoids the red zones (VRAEM and the Putumayo border area) and the orange zones (Abancay, Huánuco). France, the UK and the Netherlands name no restriction for Lima, Arequipa, Colca, Puno, Cusco or Machu Picchu. The main risks are street crime in Lima, Cusco and Arequipa, protest road blockades in the south (Cusco and Puno) after the disputed 2026 election, and rainy-season landslides and El Niño.
security.assessedRoute: Lima (Miraflores, Barranco, Surquillo, airport), Arequipa, Chivay, Colca Canyon (Cruz del Cóndor, Cabanaconde, Sangalle), Puno, Lake Titicaca islands, Cusco, Moray, Maras, Ollantaytambo, Aguas Calientes and Machu Picchu. Excludes the VRAEM, the Putumayo border, Abancay, Huánuco, the north coast under El Niño flood alerts, and Nazca overflights.

conflictRisk.note: The armed-group areas (VRAEM, Huallaga, Putumayo) are far from the route, which stays in the southern Andes and Lima.

terrorismRisk.note: Shining Path remnants are limited to coca areas such as the VRAEM; the FCDO says attacks cannot be ruled out anywhere (S04).

kidnappingRisk.note: Express kidnappings by fake taxi drivers targeting tourists are reported in cities, usually at night (S04, S08); use official or app taxis only.

regionalRestrictions: Do not enter the VRAEM, the Putumayo border zone, Abancay or Huánuco.
Do not attempt to pass blockades by road.
Nazca overflights are not part of the route (Aerodiana crash, 1 August 2026, 13 dead; S13).
Avoid central Lima after dark and the beaches in the evening (S01).
ordinaryRisks: Pickpocketing and armed robbery in Lima, Cusco and Arequipa
Bus crashes and holdups on night buses
Rainy-season landslides, flooding and train closures
Earthquakes and the Ubinas volcano near Arequipa
Dengue and other mosquito-borne illness at lower altitudes
security.medicalAccess: Good private clinics in Lima, Arequipa and Cusco; basic services at Machu Picchu and none in the Colca Canyon (S05, S06). Evacuation cover is essential.
security.insuranceConsiderations: The policy must cover trekking to 5,000 m, medical evacuation and helicopter rescue, and must not exclude regions the FCDO advises against (the route stays out of them). Some Peruvian hospitals demand upfront payment (S08).
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check France Diplomatie (zones and alerts), FCDO, Netherlands and Smartraveller/US pages before booking and two weeks before departure. Triggers: new nationwide strikes or road blockades in Cusco, Puno or Arequipa after the 2026 election; a change of the state of emergency; closure of the Machu Picchu line; a stronger-than-forecast El Niño in the southern Andes.

practicalRequirements.visa: Tourists generally need no visa for up to 90 days (UK and Dutch pages state this for their citizens); confirm for the traveller's own passport (S07, S08).
practicalRequirements.entry: Passport, return or onward ticket, and a completed immigration form on arrival; fees and digital forms can change.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least 6 months after arrival (S07, S08).

Personal medical kit and altitude medication as advised

advantages: Staged altitude route from the sea to 4,900 m before the trip peaks at Machu Picchu.
Combines a canyon trek, a lake homestay and Inca archaeology in one trip.
Does not need a rental car or camping gear.
Machu Picchu is easier to book in March than in June to August.
Machu Picchu, the Colca Canyon and Titicaca all fall in the south, so there is no need for the north coast under El Niño.
disadvantages: Long-haul flight makes the total about 2,410 EUR, in the exceptional band.
March is still the rainy season, with landslides, train closures and cloud over Machu Picchu.
Cusco and Puno have a history of protests and road blockades that can strand travellers.
Altitude sickness is a real risk for all four, and nights are cold in unheated homestays.
Many bus hours, with only one real trek and no way to self-drive.
uncertainties: Rain and landslides in the south (El Niño is forecast to be strong, but the ENFEN outlook says the south-east sierra will be drier than normal; forecasts can change).
Post-2026-election unrest, strikes and road blockades in Cusco, Puno and Arequipa; the current situation in November 2026 was not confirmed from an official source.
Official 2027 Inca Trail dates and March permit availability; official foreign-adult Machu Picchu prices; live Paris-Lima fares.
France's security zones section is dated 11 March 2026; US State Department and Smartraveller pages could not be fetched.
